sections.heading: 4.7.1 The Tic-Tac-Toe Capstone Project Architecture
sections.content:
The official Cisco NetAcad Capstone requires you to build a fully functional console Tic-Tac-Toe game where a human plays against the computer:

• Board Representation: A 3x3 list of lists representing board slots 1 through 9.
• display_board(): Pretty-prints the grid board with current moves.
• enter_move(): Prompts the user, validates that the chosen square is free, and records the move.
• victory_for(): Analyzes rows, columns, and diagonals to determine win conditions.
• draw_move(): Implements computer AI strategy to make legal moves.

Completing this project demonstrates total mastery of all concepts in Python Essentials 1.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: In a 3x3 board represented as board = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]], how do you access the center square (5)?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: In zero-based 2D indexing, row 1 and column 1 access the center element: board[1][1] is 5.

recap: You have completed Python Essentials 1! Review your projects and take the Final Examination.
